title_en: Great Poems and Songs (5/20): Su Shi and the Moon over Two Brothers
note_en: 又……又…… links two qualities or feelings that are both true at once: 又圆又亮的月亮 "a moon that was round and bright," 他心里又高兴又难过 "he felt both happy and sad." English just uses "and" or "both ... and," but Chinese puts 又 before each adjective, and leaving one out sounds wrong. The pattern works best with short adjectives and verbs, especially in pairs.

sentences.en: The two lines "People have sorrow and joy, partings and reunions; the moon is dim or bright, full or waning" have the same number of characters and a perfectly parallel structure, setting the human condition side by side with the changes of the moon. Once this neat parallelism is translated into English, the beauty of its form is very hard to preserve.
